definitions.explanation: A legal document specifying how a person's property and affairs should be handled after death. This reading is the formal legal term, as opposed to the more general ゆいごん.

examples.japanese: {遺言|いごん}を{作成|さくせい}する。
{遺言|いごん}の{内容|ないよう}が{公開|こうかい}された。
examples.english: The contents of the will were made public.

examples.japanese: {弁護士|べんごし}に{依頼|いらい}して{正式|せいしき}な{遺言|いごん}を{作成|さくせい}してもらった。
examples.english: I had a lawyer draft a formal will for me.

notes: The reading いごん is the standard legal term used in courts, law offices, and official documents. The more common reading {遺言|ゆいごん} is used in everyday speech and has a broader meaning that includes dying wishes and last words. Legal types include {自筆証書遺言|じひつしょうしょいごん} (holographic will), {公正証書遺言|こうせいしょうしょいごん} (notarial will), and {秘密証書遺言|ひみつしょうしょいごん} (sealed will). Common collocations: {遺言|いごん}を{残|のこ}す (to leave a will), {遺言|いごん}{書|しょ} (written will).

cross_references.description: General reading ゆいごん, broader meaning including dying wishes
